requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The fix lives in TypeCollector. It adds `continue` after the mixed int/string key diagnostic (MsgPack005) in both member loops (properties and fields). It also guards the int-key and string-key dictionary `Add` calls with `ContainsKey`, so duplicate or mixed keys no longer throw while the type is being collected. New analyzer tests check that a `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` type still gets MsgPack004/015/003/005, and that MsgPack011/016/017 are not reported for it. New execution tests round-trip a suppressed type. A README section documents the opt-out behaviour.
story.why: Issue 2234 says the analyzer stopped working for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types in 3.1.1. The diff implies the cause is an exception thrown during type collection: `intKey!.Value` on a null key when key kinds are mixed, and `Dictionary.Add` on duplicate keys. Such an exception would stop the analyzer for that type. The diff does not touch the analyzer entry point or any SuppressSourceGeneration-specific branch. So the claim that this is the whole root cause rests on the new analyzer tests passing, not on visible code.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section that lists which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types, including MsgPack012, which no test covers.
The duplicate-key guards also change behaviour for normal (non-suppressed) types and for the source-generator path, not only the analyzer path.
The field-member loop (lines 1144-1182) gets the same changes but no test exercises it.
story.confidence_overview: Medium. The crash-avoidance edits are small and clear. Whether they fully fix the reported regression can only be judged by the new analyzer tests passing. One execution test asserts nothing meaningful. Effects on the source-generator path (duplicate members silently dropped) are not visible in this diff.

claims.text: In the property/member loop, after reporting DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys (MsgPack005) for a member whose key kind differs from the rest, the member is skipped. This avoids the null `intKey!.Value` dereference (or null string key) that would otherwise throw.

findings.description: Claim C1 disputed: In the property loop, the string-key branch at TypeCollector.cs line 1028 is already guarded by 'else if (stringKey is not null)', so a null stringKey (!isIntKey && stringKey == null) would not throw in this loop (unlike the field loop at lines 1168-1170, which uses an unguarded 'else' and passes stringKey! to stringMembers.ContainsKey). In addition, MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure at SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 131-135 only tests an int key followed by a string key (isIntKey && intKey == null), never a string key followed by an int key.

The ContainsKey guards silently drop the second member that shares a key. On the source-generator path, if no diagnostic stops generation, a generated formatter could quietly omit that member instead of failing. Whether generation is blocked when MsgPack005 is present is not visible in this diff.

The `continue` skips all later per-member processing for a mixed-key member, including the formatter-attribute lookup at line 1045 and any later member-type checks. Other diagnostics (for example MsgPack003) on that member are no longer reported.

No change touches any SuppressSourceGeneration-specific code. If the 3.1.1 regression was an early exit for suppressed types, rather than only an exception on bad keys, this diff would not fix it. Only the passing of MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported would show the analyzer runs for valid-but-flawed suppressed types.
NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType asserts only that the resolver instance exists. It does not verify its stated behaviour.
The field-loop changes (1148, 1163-1166, 1179-1182) have no test with duplicate or mixed keys on fields.
